instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of "legislative agent" turns on being engaged to actively advocate "as one of the individual's main purposes," with no minimum compensation dollar threshold specified.
Registration is required within ten days of an engagement to actively advocate; the statute sets no expenditure dollar threshold as a trigger for registration.

Itemized reporting of meals/food/beverage expenditures per official is triggered when cumulative calendar-year payments by a legislative agent exceed $50 to or for the benefit of a particular public officer or employee.

A statement of expenditures must report total expenditures with no dollar floor, and per-official itemization under (B)(2) (non-food) applies to any expenditure made — the statute sets no minimum dollar de minimis for filing apart from the separate $50 food/beverage itemization rule.
Section 101.73 sets no time-percentage de minimis threshold for filing expenditure statements; filings are required of every registered legislative agent regardless of time spent lobbying.

arguments.justification: The statute defines a legislative agent as someone engaged "during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes" — a qualitative "main purpose" test, not a numeric time-percentage threshold.

content.text:
I'll analyze the Ohio statute for each registration/disclosure threshold.

Key findings:
- §101.70(F): "legislative agent" = engaged to actively advocate "as one of the individual's main purposes" — qualitative, no compensation/expenditure dollar threshold, no specific time percent
- §101.73(B)(3): Itemization of meals/food/beverages required when cumulative payments exceed $50 per calendar year per official
- No dollar registration threshold; no general filing de minimis dollar threshold for non-food expenditures (all must be itemized per (B)(2))

The statute defines a legislative agent as someone engaged "during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes" — a qualitative "main purpose" test, not a numeric time-percentage threshold.
